answer.content: Conduct a focused investigation of the per-interval retention metric in Section 4.1 of 'Stability and Forgetting in Autoregressive Models' by Kumar et al., 2024, to confirm its definition, measurement conditions, and variation over 100 update intervals under intermittent input and bounded token budgets. The investigation must strictly reference the original paper and exclude any extrapolation beyond the reported data points or metric scope. Acceptance criteria: the metric must be explicitly defined, quantifiable, and tied to interval-level retention under known perturbations without reference to broader model coherence or drift measures. All findings must be directly extractable from the source text and not inferred or generalized beyond the paper's stated results. No external assumptions permitted.

answer.lesson: All memory research questions must be anchored in a single, explicitly reported and verifiable metric from peer-reviewed literature before comparative analysis can proceed; unresolved validation gaps must be explicitly recorded and bounded to prevent ungrounded generalizations and ensure empirical validity in time-series analysis of agent
